summary: Let --frase express a locution that contains an Italian conjunction, instead of silently shipping it to the portal as a boolean AND.
reason: The phrase builder bailed out verbatim as soon as a token matched the ISIS operator vocabulary, so that a hand-written expression like --frase "aree E idonee" would not be rewritten. But "e" in lowercase inside a bill title is a word, not an operator: --frase "coesione e crescita" reached the engine as a plain AND over the whole document, and the flag delivered something other than what it promises with no warning anywhere. Case is the discriminator - and it only carries information when the phrase also has lowercase in it, otherwise an all-caps title pasted from the portal falls back into the same silent AND. The conjunction is dropped and the adjacency distance widened to account for it, because the engine indexes the conjunction as a position: measured on ddl 969 "prevenzione e contrasto" in legislature 18, the AND returns 144 rows, strict adjacency over the surviving words returns 3 and misses it, and the widened distance returns 41 and includes it. Quoting is not an alternative: the portal rejects a quoted term even on a single word. Only "e" and "o" are dropped: the vocabulary also contains ordinary Italian words (seguito, vicino, meno, no, escluso), and removing one of those falsifies the search rather than widening it, so a phrase containing one is shipped unchanged with a warning that the locution is not expressible.
validated_outcome: ddl cerca --legisl 18 --frase "prevenzione e contrasto" goes from 144 rows to 41, and the positive control ddl 969 is in them; the dry run reports the widened expression plus a nota_frase saying which word was dropped. Healthy homologous cases unchanged: --frase "aree idonee" still builds (aree adj idonee), --testo keeps its AND, --frase "aree E idonee" stays verbatim. Live dogfood 127 tests, 0 fail. A phrase carrying a full word from the vocabulary is left alone: --frase "aree meno idonee" still builds (aree meno idonee), with the warning.
